prompt:
Thomas the factory designer has two machines, S and P, designed for crafting electronic circuits. Electronic circuits take copper wires and iron plates to craft. Machine S crafts 1 circuit every second, consuming 4 copper wires and 3 iron plates per craft. Machine P crafts 1 circuit every 1.6 seconds, consuming 3 copper wires and 2 iron plates per craft.

Thomas has a supply of 18300 copper wires and an excess of iron plates. He must produce at least 5000 circuits to meet his manager's quota. He wants to produce these circuits as quickly as possible, but due to a power shortage, it is not possible for him to run both machines simultaneously. What is the minimum amount of time, in minutes, that it takes for him to produce the circuits needed? Express your answer as a decimal number rounded to the nearest 10th.

solutions.title: Linear optimization
solutions.body:
Let $S$ craft $x$ circuits and $P$ craft $y$ circuits with $x+y=5000$ (making more is only slower). The copper constraint is $4x+3y=15000+x\le18300$, so $x\le3300$. Since the machines cannot run together, the time is $x+1.6y=x+1.6(5000-x)=8000-0.6x$ seconds, which is smallest for the largest $x$, namely $x=3300$: $8000-1980=6020$ seconds.

In minutes: $\frac{6020}{60}\approx100.33$, which rounds to $100.3$.

**Answer: 100.3**

prompt: Six basketball teams participate in a single round-robin tournament. That is, each pair of teams play one game against each other, with one team winning and the other losing. The teams are all mutually equally matched: in any game, the chance each team has of winning is exactly $\frac12$. Compute the probability that there are two teams that win the same number of games over the course of the tournament.

solutions.title: Complement
solutions.body:
Find the probability that all six win totals are different. Each team plays $5$ games, so the possible win totals are $0,1,\dots,5$, and six distinct totals must be exactly $\{0,1,2,3,4,5\}$ in some order: $6!=720$ assignments of totals to teams. (Each such assignment is realized by exactly one outcome: the team with $5$ wins beats everyone, the team with $4$ wins beats everyone except the $5$-win team, and so on.)

There are $2^{15}$ equally likely outcomes of the $15$ games, so the probability that all totals are distinct is $\frac{720}{2^{15}}=\frac{45}{2048}$. Hence the answer is $1-\frac{45}{2048}=\frac{2003}{2048}$.

**Answer: $\frac{2003}{2048}$**

prompt:
Find the number of ordered 6-tuples of integers
$$(x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,y_2,y_3),\qquad\text{with }0\le x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,y_2,y_3\le9,$$
such that $(x_1-y_1)+2(x_2-y_2)+3(x_3-y_3)$ is divisible by $7$.

solutions.title: Base-10 trick
solutions.body:
Since $10\equiv3\pmod7$, we have $10^0\equiv1$, $10^1\equiv3$, $10^2\equiv2$, $10^3\equiv6\equiv-1$, $10^4\equiv-3$, $10^5\equiv-2$. Read the six digits as the number $n=\overline{y_2y_3y_1x_2x_3x_1}$. Then
$$n\equiv-2y_2-3y_3-y_1+2x_2+3x_3+x_1=(x_1-y_1)+2(x_2-y_2)+3(x_3-y_3)\pmod 7.$$
The $6$-tuples correspond bijectively to the integers $0\le n<10^6$, so we count multiples of $7$ in $[0,10^6)$: since $10^6-1=7\cdot142857$, there are $142857+1=142858$ of them (including $0$).

**Answer: 142858**
